content:
**Blocked: no web access available.** I could not perform the research.

## Tool failure report

Every network-capable tool returned the same permission error, with no way to approve it:

| Tool | Call attempted | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `websearch` | `"test"` (trivial verification query) | `permission required but no prompt available for websearch` |
| `websearch` | `Federico Lauria doctoral dissertation philosophy desire secrecy loneliness` | `permission required but no prompt available for websearch` |
| `webfetch` | DuckDuckGo HTML search URL | `permission required but no prompt available for webfetch` |
| `webfetch` | Google search URL | `permission required but no prompt available for webfetch` |
| `bash` | `curl -s https://duckduckgo.com/` (fallback attempt) | `permission required but no prompt available for bash` |
| `bash` | `echo hello` (confirm not network-specific) | `permission required but no prompt available for bash` |

Read-only local tools do work (`glob` ran fine and returned no matches — this project directory has no `.md` files, so there is nothing local to consult either).

Note that `echo hello` failing shows the block is not limited to network calls: **`bash` is entirely unavailable**, so there is no curl/wget fallback path either.

## What I am deliberately not doing

I am not reporting a dissertation title, an institution, a footnote 397 citation, or any SAAM search results. Answering those would require recalling them from training data, and the three sub-questions form a chain — the referenced work at footnote 397 determines which chapter titles to search for at SAAM — so a single unverified guess would silently corrupt everything downstream. There is also a real risk of confabulation here: the prompt itself offers several candidate titles ("The Logic of the Secret", Columbia vs. Geneva) and a subject cluster (desire/secrecy/loneliness), which is exactly the shape of question where a plausible-sounding answer is easy to invent and hard to distinguish from a retrieved one.

## To unblock

Grant permission for `websearch` and `webfetch` (and ideally `bash`, for direct PDF fetches of the dissertation and the SAAM API), then re-send the task. With those available, the plan is:

1. Locate the dissertation record and its full-text PDF (institutional repository / ProQuest / the author's academia.edu or Geneva UNIGE page), confirming author, year, and committee to rule out a different Federico Lauria.
2. Jump to footnote 397 and quote it verbatim, cross-checking against a second copy of the text if one exists, since footnote numbering can shift between a submitted and a published version.
3. Query the SAAM collections API (`api.si.edu`) for paintings whose titles match chapter headings of that work, and report each hit with its object page URL.
